title: A New $50 Deal for Weight Loss Meds—But There's a Catch
summary:
Have you heard of medicines like Wegovy or Zepbound? They help people lose weight, but they can cost hundreds of dollars a month. That's a big problem, because about half of the people who take them say they're hard to afford.

Now, there's good news: Starting July 1, 2026, a new Medicare program called the GLP-1 Bridge will let some people get these drugs for only $50 per prescription. That's way cheaper! But it's not for everyone. You must have Medicare Part D, and your body mass index (BMI) must be 27 or higher with a health problem like heart disease, or 35 and above.

Here's the catch: The program ends in December 2027. After that, the price might go way up again. Also, the $50 you pay won't count toward your Medicare deductible or out-of-pocket limit. And if you get extra help paying for medicines, you can't use it for this program.

Doctors say these drugs work best if you keep taking them. If you stop, you might regain the weight. So the short program worries some experts. Still, for many people, $50 a month is a huge relief. If you think you might qualify, talk to your doctor soon!
why_it_matters: If an adult in your family is struggling with weight and worried about costs, programs like this could help them talk to a doctor and get medicine they might otherwise skip.

background_read: Medicare is a U.S. government program that provides health coverage to people 65 and older and some with disabilities. It has different parts – Part D helps pay for prescription medicines.
Drugs like Wegovy and Zepbound mimic a natural hormone called GLP-1 that tells your brain you're full. They can be very effective but often cost over $1,000 a month without insurance.
A person's body mass index (BMI) is a number doctors use to screen for weight problems; a BMI of 27 or higher is considered overweight, and 35 or higher is severe obesity.
Article_Structure: WHO: People with Medicare Part D and high BMI, doctors, and the Medicare program.
WHAT: A temporary new program called GLP-1 Bridge that cuts the price of weight-loss drugs to $50 per prescription.
WHERE: In the United States, for Medicare Part D members who qualify.
WHY: Because many people can't afford these effective medicines, and high prices stop them from staying on the treatment.

perspectives.description: The $50 price is a huge relief for many who couldn't afford these drugs. It gives people a chance to start treatment and improve their health.
The program ends quickly in 2027, and the $50 payments don't help reach the out-of-pocket limit. If someone can't afford the full price later, they might lose progress.
Weight-loss drugs are not a short-term fix – studies show most people regain weight if they stop. Experts worry that a temporary program doesn't match the long-term need.
